name: Custom Portfolio Website (This Site)
tagline: A data-driven portfolio built from scratch.
short_description: A fully responsive, accessible, and themeable portfolio website built to showcase my skills in modern web development practices.

details.story: This portfolio serves as a real-world demonstration of my development skills and evolution. It began as a custom-built site using vanilla PHP to showcase my foundational understanding of web principles. It was then completely rebuilt using the Laravel framework to demonstrate my ability to work with modern, professional-grade tools and best practices. name: PowerShell DOCX to Markdown Converter
tagline: An advanced script for automating writing workflows.
short_description: A sophisticated PowerShell script that uses Pandoc to convert structured Microsoft Word documents into a nested, multi-file Markdown project, perfect for personal wikis or static site generators.

details.story: To manage a large, multi-generational fictional universe, I needed an automated way to convert my primary writing files from Microsoft Word into a structured set of Markdown files suitable for my Obsidian vault and for web publishing. This script is the engine that powers that workflow.
features: Processes single files or entire directories of .docx files.
Automatically creates a nested folder structure based on Heading 1, 2, and 3 styles (Book/Chapter/Part).
Parses YAML frontmatter from the source Word document and preserves it.
Intelligently generates 'previous' and 'next' navigation links in the frontmatter of each chapter.
Includes robust command-line parameters for configuration (-Padding, -PurgeOutputFolder) and a full help screen.

name: StoreTrainer
tagline: A Utility for Launching PC Game Trainers
short_description: A custom tool for creating shortcuts that launch two executables at once (e.g., a game and a trainer) and correctly sets the Working Directory.

details.story: StoreTrainer was born out of a classic PC gaming problem from the late 90s. As my first Windows binary executable, created in 1998 with Visual Basic 6.0, it solved a personal annoyance: launching a game and a separate 'trainer' application simultaneously. The codebase is still maintained in Windows NT 4.0 and Windows 2000 virtual machines, a testament to its legacy roots. The tool creates a single shortcut that not only launches both programs but, more importantly, correctly sets the 'Working Directory' for each—a common point of failure that often prevented trainers from working correctly. It's a practical utility that demonstrates a foundational understanding of the Windows application environment and a long-standing passion for building tools that solve real-world problems.
features: Creates a single shortcut to launch two separate executables.
Correctly resolves and sets the 'Working Directory' for each application.
Provides a simple, user-friendly interface for creating and managing shortcuts.
Demonstrates remarkable backward and forward compatibility.
compatibility: Tested and fully functional on modern 64-bit Windows 11 Pro, including the ARM version running in a VM on Apple Silicon.

name: RaggieSoft Presentation Software
short_description: Engineered to overcome a mobility impairment during a university class, this web-based software featured separate presenter and audience views, enabling seamless presentation from an iPad before mainstream mobile solutions were common.

details.story: Typically, at the time, presentations given in the front of the classroom involved creating Microsoft PowerPoint presentations, saving them to a USB stick, and running them from the instructor's computer which was connected to the projector. Typically, my classmates would turn their heads back to read the PowerPoint presentations, then turn back towards the class. Being mobility impaired, I was unable to turn myself to look at the presentation to remember what I needed to say. So I crafted a web application designed to run on an iPad, and used Apple's Lightning to HDMI adapter to plug the iPad into the classroom's display console for the projector (this was in the days before wirelessly streaming content from a mobile device to a display). I could then read the notes on my iPad while facing the class, with my presentation displaying on the projector screen for the class to see, without straining my neck due to a mobility impairment.
features: Web-based system accessible from any device with a browser.
Separate, synchronized views for the presenter (with notes) and the audience (slides only).
Enabled seamless presentation from an iPad using a Lightning to HDMI adapter.
Developed as a practical accessibility solution before mainstream mobile presentation tools were common.
